# PART I: Foundations of LBBNN & Input-Skip Architecture (ISLaB)

## Motivation — Why Sparse & Explainable BNNs in Official Statistics?

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Challenges with Standard Deep Learning in Federal Agencies:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Standard deep neural networks capture complex non-linearities and multi-way interactions, but are massively over-parameterized, black-box, and lack reliable uncertainty quantification.
  \item Standard dense Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) quantify weight uncertainty, but retain all extraneous noise variables, causing severe variance inflation in downstream survey estimators.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Our Core Objectives with \texttt{LBBNN} \& \texttt{ISLaB}:}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Joint Structural \& Parameter Uncertainty}: Unify spike-and-slab topological edge selection with variational weight distributions in a single probabilistic framework.
  \item \textbf{Dynamic Adaptation (Depth Metric)}: Automatically adapt between simple linear models ($\text{Depth} = 1$) and deep non-linear interaction surfaces ($\text{Depth} \ge 2$).
  \item \textbf{Federal Statistical Extensions}: Extend \texttt{LBBNN} to handle informative survey sampling weights, $(\epsilon, \delta)$-differential privacy, and non-probability sample integration.
\end{enumerate}

## From Dense BNNs to Latent Binary BNNs (LBBNNs)

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Probabilistic Formulation (Hubin \& Storvik, 2024):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Likelihood $y_i \sim f(\cdot \mid \zeta(\mathbf{x}_i))$, where hidden layer pre-activations include binary inclusion indicators:
  $$a_p^{(j)} = o^{(j)}\!\left(w_{0,p}^{(j)} + \sum_{k=1}^{K} \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)} a_k^{(j-1)} w_{k,p}^{(j)}\right), \qquad \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)} \in \{0, 1\}$$
  \item \textbf{Spike-and-Slab Structural Prior}:
  $$p\big(w_{k,p}^{(j)} \mid \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big) = \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)} \mathcal{N}\big(0, (\tau_{k,p}^{(j)})^2\big) + \big(1 - \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big)\delta_0, \qquad p\big(\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big) = \text{Bernoulli}\big(\psi_{k,p}^{(j)}\big)$$
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Inference \& Dual Operational Modes:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA)}: Ensembles across posterior draws $\Gamma \sim q(\Gamma)$ and $W \sim q(W \mid \Gamma)$ for optimal uncertainty quantification and predictive calibration.
  \item \textbf{Median Probability Model (MPM)}: Hard-prunes all edges whose posterior inclusion probability $\alpha_{k,p}^{(j)} = \mathbb{P}(\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)} = 1 \mid \mathcal{D}) \le 0.5$ (Barbieri \& Berger, 2004 optimal predictive submodel).
\end{itemize}

## Input-Skip LBBNNs (ISLaB) & Structural Depth Metrics

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.54\textwidth}
\textbf{The ISLaB Architecture (H{\o}yheim et al., 2026, \textit{JAIR}):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Direct skips route inputs $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ to all hidden layers: $\mathbf{a}^{(j-1)} = [a_1^{(j-1)}, \dots, a_K^{(j-1)}, \mathbf{x}^\top]^\top$.
  \item \textbf{Active Paths ($\text{AP}$)}: Connects input $x_k$ to output $\zeta$ if all intermediate edges have $\alpha_{k,p}^{(j)} > 0.5$.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Contribution Depth Classification:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Depth = 1}: Input-to-output skip $\implies$ Linear GLM effect.
  \item \textbf{Depth $\ge$ 2}: Through hidden nodes $\implies$ Non-linear/interaction.
  \item \textbf{Zero Paths ($L = 0$)}: Covariate completely pruned.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.46\textwidth}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.68, every node/.style={scale=0.68}]

## Local Explainability via Piecewise-Linear Activation Regions

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Local Generalized Linear Model Representation (Hubin et al., JSM 2026):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item With continuous piecewise-linear activations (e.g., ReLU), the input space $\mathbb{R}^p$ is partitioned into a finite set of convex polyhedral activation regions $\mathcal{P}_1, \dots, \mathcal{P}_M$.
  \item Within any local neighborhood $B_\epsilon(\mathbf{x}_i) \subset \mathcal{P}_m$, the active network collapses to an exact \textbf{local Generalized Linear Model (GLM)}:
  $$\zeta(\mathbf{x}) = \beta_0(\mathbf{x}_i) + \sum_{j=1}^p \beta_j(\mathbf{x}_i) x_j, \qquad \boldsymbol{\beta}(\mathbf{x}_i) = \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \zeta(\mathbf{x})\big|_{\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{x}_i}$$
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{Rigorous Statistical Properties for Official Statistics:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Closed-Form Gradients}: Local coefficients $\beta_j(\mathbf{x}_i)$ are evaluated exactly via backpropagation without numerical perturbation approximations (e.g., unlike LIME or Kernel SHAP).
  \item \textbf{Bayesian Local Credible Intervals}: Sampling posterior weights $W \sim q(W \mid \Gamma^*)$ yields exact posterior distributions $p(\boldsymbol{\beta}(\mathbf{x}_i) \mid \mathcal{D})$ for local covariate effects on individual survey respondents.
\end{itemize}

## Variational ELBO, Cold-Posterior Protection & Software Ecosystem

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.55\textwidth}
\textbf{Variational Inference Framework:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Mean-field spike-and-slab: $q(\mathbf{w}, \boldsymbol{\gamma}) = \prod q(w_{k,p}^{(j)} \mid \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}) \, q(\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)})$.
  \item Efficient sampling via Local Reparameterization Trick (LRT) and Normalizing Flows (\textit{TMLR}, 2024).
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Protection Against Cold Posteriors (Wenzel et al., 2020):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Exact ELBO at $T = 1.0$: $\text{ELBO}(q) = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}_{q}[\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)] - \text{KL}(q \parallel p)$.
  \item Explicit observation noise $\sigma^2$ in Gaussian regression (\texttt{sigma} in \texttt{lbbnn\_net()}) prevents likelihood mis-scaling ($T = \sigma^2 \neq 1$) and protects spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.45\textwidth}
\textbf{Open-Source Software Ecosystem:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{R Package \texttt{LBBNN}}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Available on CRAN (v0.1.6).
      \item Built on \texttt{torch} for R (pure C++ LibTorch backend, zero Python overhead).
      \item Exported helpers for dataloaders, survey weighting, and custom likelihoods.
    \end{itemize}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \item \textbf{Python Package \texttt{ISLaB-LBBNN}}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item PyTorch implementation supporting large-scale GPU cluster distributed training.
    \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

# PART II: Track 1 — Unit-Weighted Pseudo-Posteriors & Formal Differential Privacy

## Track 1 Overview — Unit-Weighted Variational Pseudo-Posteriors

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{BLS Collaboration with Terrance D. Savitsky, Matthew R. Williams \& Vladislav Beresovsky:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Equipping each unit $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$ with a non-negative weight $u_i \ge 0$ defines the variational pseudo-posterior (Savitsky \& Toth, 2016; Bhattacharya et al., 2019):
  $$p_{\mathbf{u}}(\theta \mid \mathbf{y}) \propto p(\theta) \prod_{i=1}^n f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)^{u_i} \iff \text{ELBO}(q; \mathbf{u}) = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i \, \mathbb{E}_{q(\theta)}[\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)] - \text{KL}(q \parallel p)$$
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Two Distinct Operational Regimes Implemented in \texttt{LBBNN}:}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Survey Sampling Weights ($u_i = \tilde{w}_i$)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Design weights $w_i = \pi_i^{-1}$ are sample-size normalized: $\tilde{w}_i = w_i \frac{n}{\sum_{j=1}^n w_j}$ (\texttt{normalize\_weights = TRUE}).
      \item Enforces $\sum \tilde{w}_i = n$, ensuring the data likelihood does not overpower the spike-and-slab KL penalty.
    \end{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Differential Privacy Weights ($u_i = \alpha_i \in [0, 1]$)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Risk-downweighting factors are left unnormalized (\texttt{normalize\_weights = FALSE}, $\sum \alpha_i \le n$).
      \item Downweights high-sensitivity tail outliers and contracts the pseudo-posterior toward the prior.
    \end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}

## Survey-Weighted Imputation Under Informative Sampling (Setup)

\vspace{0.1em}
\textbf{True Non-Linear DGP}: $Y_i = 2.0 X_{1i} + 1.5 \sin(\pi X_{2i}) + 0.8 X_{1i} X_{2i} + \varepsilon_i$, $\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.4^2)$, $X_3, X_4 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.46\textwidth}
\textbf{Simulation Setup ($N = 2,000, p = 4$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Informative Selection Mechanism}:
  $$\pi_i = \text{logit}^{-1}(-1.0 + 1.2 Y_i)$$
  Draws $n = 737$ units favoring high $Y_i$.
  \item Biased sample mean: \textbf{+2.009} (True: \textbf{0.000}).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

## Two-Pass $(\epsilon, \delta)$-Differential Privacy (Savitsky et al., 2022)

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Why Unweighted Neural Networks Fail DP on Skewed Survey Data:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Pointwise log-likelihood $|\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)| \propto \frac{(y_i - \mu_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i))^2}{2\sigma^2}$ grows \textbf{quadratically} with the residual.
  \item In skewed expenditure/income data, extreme outliers drive local sensitivity $\Delta \to \infty$, destroying privacy.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{The Two-Pass Surgical Mechanism (\texttt{fit\_dp\_lbbnn}):}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Pass 1 (Exploration)}: Fit unweighted LBBNN ($u_i = 1$). Extract $S \times n$ matrix $L_{s,i}^{(1)} = \log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta^{(1,s)})$ via \texttt{loglik\_contributions()}, and evaluate worst-case sensitivity $f_i = \max_s |L_{s,i}^{(1)}|$.
  \item \textbf{Monotone Surgical Weights}: Compute smooth risk weights $\alpha_i^{\text{raw}} = c_{\text{scale}}(1 - \tilde{f}_i)$, cap at $\alpha_i \leftarrow \min(\alpha_i^{\text{raw}}, M_{\text{thresh}}/f_i)$, and \textbf{surgically zero extreme tail outliers}:
  $$\alpha_i = 0 \quad \text{if } f_i > 3 M_{\text{thresh}}$$
  \item \textbf{Pass 2 ($\boldsymbol{\alpha}$-Weighted Fit \& Synthesis)}: Fit LBBNN with $u_i = \alpha_i$. Verify local Lipschitz bound $\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}} = \max_{s,i} |\alpha_i L_{s,i}^{(2)}| \le M_{\text{thresh}}$ and privacy budget $\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} = 2\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}}$.
  \item \textbf{Microdata Synthesis}: Draw synthetic records via the \textbf{DP Post-Processing Theorem}.
\end{enumerate}

# PART III: Track 2 — Combining Probability & Non-Probability Samples

## Track 2 Overview — Selection Bias & The Conditioning Trick

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Collaboration with Vladislav Beresovsky, Julie Gershunskaya \& Terrance D. Savitsky (2026):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{The Big Data Paradox (Meng, 2018)}: Opt-in convenience samples $S_c$ suffer from severe selection bias:
  $$\text{Bias}(\bar{y}_c) \approx \rho_{R, Y} \cdot \sigma_Y \cdot \sqrt{\frac{N - n_c}{n_c}}$$
  Massive convenience sample size $n_c$ merely shrinks variance around an egregiously biased estimate.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{The Identification Barrier \& The Conditioning Trick:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Barrier}: Covariates $\mathbf{x}_i$ are observed only for $i \in S_c$ ($R_i = 1$, unknown $\pi_{ci}$) and for a reference probability survey $S_r$ ($I_i = 1$, known design probability $\pi_{ri}$), never on $U \setminus (S_c \cup S_r)$.
  \item \textbf{Conditioning Trick}: By pooling $S_c$ and $S_r$ and conditioning on selection into the combined sample $S$, the known reference design probability $\pi_{ri}$ acts as a \textbf{structural offset} that anchors neural network logits $\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i)$ to the true population scale:
  $$\pi_{zi} = \mathbb{P}(i \in S_c \mid i \in S_c \cup S_r, \mathbf{x}_i) = \frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$$
\end{itemize}

## Five Sample Combination Formulations (Beresovsky et al., 2026)

\vspace{0.1em}
\scriptsize
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{p{1.8cm}p{3.0cm}p{3.0cm}p{4.8cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Estimator} & \textbf{Sample Domain} & \textbf{Target Indicator} & \textbf{Composite Probability $\pi_{zi}$} \\
\midrule
\texttt{STACK} & $S_c \oplus S_r$ (Unlinked) & $I_{zi} = D_i$ (sample source) & $\frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$ \\
\texttt{LINK1} & $S_c \cup (S_r \setminus S_c)$ & $I_{zi} = I_{ci}$ (deduplicated) & $\frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri} - \pi_{ci}\pi_{ri}}$ \\
\texttt{LINK2} & $S_c \oplus S_r$ (Linked) & $I_{zi} = D_i + (1-D_i)I_{ci}$ & $\frac{\pi_{ci}(1 + \pi_{ri})}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$ \\
\texttt{MIP} & Missing Information & $\tilde{I}_{zi}^{\text{MIP}} = D_i + (1-D_i)\tilde{p}_i$ & Bridges \texttt{STACK} ($p=0$) and \texttt{LINK2} ($p=1$) \\
\texttt{PSEUDO} & Survey Weighted & Score: $\nabla \ell_{\text{pseudo}} = 0$ & Design-weighted: $\sum_{S_r} \pi_{ri}^{-1} \text{softplus}(\eta_i)$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\normalsize

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Structural Characteristics:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Deterministic Linkage (\texttt{LINK1}, \texttt{LINK2})}: Utilizes unit-level linkage overlap between $S_c$ and $S_r$ to maximize Fisher information and minimize asymptotic variance.
  \item \textbf{Missing Information Principle (\texttt{MIP})}: Continuously bridges unlinked \texttt{STACK} ($p_{\text{link}} = 0$) and fully linked \texttt{LINK2} ($p_{\text{link}} = 1$) via EM expectations.
  \item \textbf{Pseudo-Likelihood (\texttt{PSEUDO})}: Vulnerable to catastrophic weight explosion when reference probabilities $\pi_{ri} \approx 0$.
\end{itemize}

## Study 1 — Automated Confounder Selection & Noise Pruning ($p = 6$)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
\textbf{Simulation Setup ($N = 5,000, p = 6$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Confounders}: $X_1, X_2$ drive both propensity $\pi_{ci}$ and outcome $Y_i$.
  \item \textbf{Outcome-Only}: $X_3$ drives $Y_i$ but not $\pi_{ci}$.
  \item \textbf{Pure Noise}: $X_4, X_5, X_6 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Why Feature Selection Matters}:
\begin{itemize}
  \item In standard GLMs, including outcome-only or noise predictors in propensity models inflates H\'{a}jek weight variance without reducing confounding bias.
  \item \texttt{LBBNN} automatically prunes non-propensity predictors.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.56\textwidth}
\textbf{Variational Edge Probabilities (Table 4):}

\scriptsize
```{r}
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Variable = c("X1 (Active)", "X2 (Active)", "X3 (Outcome)", "X4 (Noise)", "X5 (Noise)", "X6 (Noise)"),
    Role = c("Confounder", "Confounder", "Outcome Only", "Pure Noise", "Pure Noise", "Pure Noise"),
    "Out Incl." = pres_data$t2_sim1_var_sel[["Output Incl."]],
    Status = c("Selected", "Selected", "Pruned", "Pruned", "Pruned", "Pruned"),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  format = "latex",
  booktabs = TRUE,
  digits = 3
)
```
\normalsize

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Active confounders $X_1, X_2$ selected ($a_1 \ge 0.99$).
  \item $X_3$ and noise $X_4\text{--}X_6$ completely pruned ($a_1 \le 0.038$).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Study 2 — High Common Support with Non-Linear Propensity & Interaction

\vspace{0.1em}
\textbf{Non-Linear DGP Surface}: $\eta_c(\mathbf{x}_i) = \beta_0 + 1.0 X_{1i} - 0.5 X_{2i} + 1.2 X_{1i}X_{2i} + \cos(\pi X_{1i}) - 0.8 X_{2i}^2$

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}

\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\textbf{Key Insights}:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Even under high common support, linear GLMs are \textbf{structurally misspecified}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \texttt{GLM-LINK1} bias: \textbf{-0.388}
      \item \texttt{GLM-LINK2} bias: \textbf{-0.393}
      \item \texttt{GLM-PSEUDO} bias: \textbf{-0.389}
    \end{itemize}
  \item \textbf{LBBNN Non-Linear Recovery}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Hidden layer captures $X_1 X_2$ interaction and trigonometric curvature.
      \item \texttt{LBBNN-STACK (MPM)} bias: \textbf{-0.086} (4.5x reduction!).
      \item \texttt{LBBNN-LINK2 (MPM)} bias: \textbf{-0.297}.
    \end{itemize}
  \item Prunes noise features $X_3\text{--}X_6$ ($a_1 \le 0.066$).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

\textbf{Catastrophic Breakdown of PSEUDO:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item When $\pi_{ci}$ is high where $\pi_{ri} \approx 0$, pseudo weights $w_i = \pi_{ri}^{-1}$ explode.
  \item \textbf{Kish ESS collapses to 6.56} (out of $n_c = 521$!), causing bias to blow up to \textbf{+5.057}.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.3em}
\textbf{Composite LBBNN Robustness:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Relative odds $\pi_{zi} = \frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$ bound gradients.
  \item \textbf{\texttt{LBBNN-LINK2 (MPM)}} achieves lowest bias (\textbf{+0.608}) and highest effective sample size (\textbf{Kish ESS = 135.98}).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

# PART IV: Unified Software Architecture & Synthesis

## Unified LBBNN Architecture Across Track 1 & Track 2

\vspace{0.1em}
\scriptsize
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{p{3.6cm}p{2.7cm}p{6.8cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Function / Module} & \textbf{Operational Track} & \textbf{Description \& Statistical Role} \\
\midrule
\texttt{get\_dataloaders()} & Track 1 \& 2 & Handles non-trainable weights $u_i \ge 0$, normalization, and multi-targets. \\
\texttt{lbbnn\_net(sigma, ...)} & Track 1 \& 2 & ELBO likelihood scaling by error variance $\sigma^2$ (cold-posterior protection). \\
\texttt{loglik\_contributions()} & Track 1B (Privacy) & Computes $S \times n$ record-level log-likelihood contributions $L_{s, i}$. \\
\texttt{fit\_dp\_lbbnn()} & Track 1B (Privacy) & Two-pass monotone surgical downweighting with Lipschitz bound $\Delta_{\alpha}$. \\
\texttt{sample\_synthetic\_lbbnn()} & Track 1B (Privacy) & Generates $(\epsilon, \delta)$-DP synthetic microdata via post-processing theorem. \\
\midrule
\texttt{nll\_link1()} / \texttt{nll\_link2()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Composite Bernoulli NLL on singly matched and matched-pair samples. \\
\texttt{make\_nll\_mip(p\_link)} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Factory producing composite NLL under Missing Information Principle. \\
\texttt{nll\_stack()} / \texttt{nll\_pseudo()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Stacked pooled sample NLL and survey design-weighted pseudo-NLL. \\
\texttt{build\_propensity\_dataset()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Formats covariates and targets for any of the 5 estimation methods. \\
\texttt{hajek\_estimate()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Computes self-normalizing H\'{a}jek estimator $\sum w_i y_i / \sum w_i$ with $w_i = \hat{\pi}_{ci}^{-1}$. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\normalsize

## Key Takeaways & Synthesis for Official Statistics

\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Survey-Weighted Pseudo-Posteriors (Track 1A)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Normalizing survey weights to sample size ($\sum \tilde{w}_i = n$) + calibrated observation noise $\sigma^2$ prevents likelihood mis-scaling ($T \neq 1$) and protects spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
      \item \texttt{LBBNN} achieves 5x lower population RMSE than classical H\'{a}jek weighting under informative sampling while pruning irrelevant covariates.
    \end{itemize}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \item \textbf{Two-Pass $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PDP Microdata Synthesis (Track 1B)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Monotone surgical downweighting (\texttt{fit\_dp\_lbbnn}) eliminates disclosure risk from extreme tail outliers ($\alpha_i = 0$) while preserving high utility ($\alpha_i \in [0.34, 0.85]$) on normal records.
    \end{itemize}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \item \textbf{Composite Non-Probability Sample Integration (Track 2)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Conditioning on pooled sample inclusion $S_c \cup S_r$ allows known design probabilities $\pi_{ri}$ to anchor neural network logits to the true population scale.
      \item Composite Bernoulli likelihoods (\texttt{LINK2}, \texttt{LINK1}, \texttt{MIP}, \texttt{STACK}) bound loss gradients and prevent the catastrophic effective sample size collapse (\texttt{Kish ESS} $< 7$) of pseudo-likelihood under low common support.
    \end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}
